Kalyabdhiyānamīmāṃsā
by Nṛsiṁha, Kāśi, of Śrīraṅgagiri.
Pt.. Madras, 1885. See Br. Mus. Pt.. Bk.. 1876-92. 26.

Kalyala
one of the divisions according to the Rāṇāyanīya recension of the Sv. listed in Caraṇavyūha.
See TD. 1763.

Kalyalakṣmīnṛsiṃha
poet. pupil of Ahobalasudhī. See NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 240.
--Anyoktimālā or Kavikaumudī.
--Janakajānanda nāṭaka. Skt. Col.. Mys. p. 6.

Kalyāṇa
prince of Patrapuñja in Antarvedi (between the Jumna an. the Ganges), son of King Vīravara an. pupil of Śeṣa Kṛṣṇa; for whom Kṛṣṇa wrote the C. Prakāśa on Prakriyākaumudī (beg. of 17th Cent. A. D.). Adyar D. VI. 155.
See also Ind. Ant. 41. p. 252.

Kalyāṇa
teacher of Nandalāla (C. on Yogaśataka. med. Bomb. Uni. 302).

Kalyāṇa
father of Rājarṣi, a. of Yoginīdaśā or Daśācintāmaṇi, C.. IX. 109. L. 2970.

Kalyāṇa
Sanskrit form of the name Kalhaṇa, a. of Rājataraṅgiṇī. See below.

Kalyāṇa
Jain.
--Kalikuṇḍapārśvastuti or Kalikuṇḍagīta. BORI. D. XIX. i. 79.
See above Kaliº.

Kalyāṇa
--Gargarakṣāvidhāna. IM. 5695.

Kalyāṇa
--Gītagaṅgādhara, a devotional poem in 12 Cantos, in imitation of Jayadeva's Gītagovinda. BBRAS. 1186. Oxf. 129a. [Page249-a.

Kalyāṇa
--Tithikalpadruma. jy. BBRAS. 236. IO. 2962.

Kalyāṇa
--Virudāvalī (a. alliterative panegyric in prose an. verse). C.. VI. 142.

Kalyāṇa
--C. on Anuttaratriṁśikā, ref. to by Abhinavagupta in his Tantrāloka, Vol. VIII, Āh. 13. p. 96.
See K. C. Pandey, Abhinavagupta (1963), p. 911 an. NCC. I. Revised edn. p. 201b.

Kalyāṇa
Jain.
--C. composed in 1629 A. D. on Yugapradhānasvarūpa. See J. Klatt, ‘Eine Apokryphe Paṭṭāvali der Jainas’, Festgruss a. Otto von Bohtlingk, p.. 54 ff. Stuttgart (Also Guerinot 659).

Kalyāṇa
or kalyANajI
--Agniṣṭomaprayogaṭippaṇa. NW. 8.
--Āśvalāyanasūtraṭippaṇa. NW. 10.
--Kātyāyanasūtraṭippaṇa. NW. 10.
--Pavamānaṭippaṇa. NW. 8.
--Puruṣasūktaṭippaṇa. NW. 8.
--Rātrisūktaṭippaṇa. NW. 8.

Kalyāṇa
son of Mahīdhara (a. of Mantramahodadhi) an. grandson of Rāmadāsa (son of Ratnākara).
--Bālatantra or Bālacikitsā. med. composed in 1587 A. D. Bomb. Uni. 216. L. 818. Mu7nchen J. 398.
See JASB. 1907, p. 213. Ref. to by his father Mahīdhara a. having helped in the composition of his Mantramahodadhi, composed in 1589 A. D. [Page249-b] See Gode, Stud. in Ind. Lit. His.. II. p.. 114-21.

Kalyāṇa_?
Jain.
--Vīrastava. BORI. D. XIX. ii. 473.

Kalyāṇa_Upādhyāya_(śarman)
flourished in Mithilā under Rāghavasiṁha of the Karṇāṭa dynasty, 18th Cent. A. D.
--Kāvyaprakāśavyākhyā-Kalpalatā.
--Durgāpūjāpaddhati. Mithilā.
--Nityārcanāvidhi. Mithilā.
--Śivapratiṣṭhāpaddhati. CPB. 5738. Mithilā I. 364.
--Śuśliṣṭapariśiṣṭa. Mithilā.
--Verses of his q. in Vidyākarasahasraka; see p.. 70. 73. 84. 85. 98. 111.
See G. Jha, Kāvyaprakāśa, English transl., Intro. p. 9; Intro., Vidyākarasahasraka, p. 4; Kane, HDS. I. p. 684b; V. Raghavan, J. of the Uni. of Madras XXVIII. ii. p. 191.

Kalyāṇaṛṣi

Pt.. Bombay, 1871. See IO. Pt.. Bk.. 1936, p. 1234.

Kalyāṇaka
surname of Melagiri ācārya, father of Koneri Bhaṭṭa (a. of Āśaucanirṇaya).

Kalyāṇaka

Kalyāṇakandastuti(kallāṇakandastotra)
Jain. Pkt. Pādapūrtikāvya by Caturavijaya, disciple of Kāntivijaya.

Kalyāṇakaprakaraṇa

Kalyāṇakallola

Kalyāṇakavidhi

Kalyāṇakāṇḍa

Kalyāṇakāma

Kalyāṇakāraka
med. by Ugrāditya or Ugrācārya, pupil of Śrīnandin; written a. Rāmagiri of Vengi during the reign of the Cālūkya king Viṣṇuvardhana IV (790-799 A. D.).
Arrah II. 20. Burnell 66a. Moodbidri I. 28. Mysore I. p.. 362 (5 mss.). 650. Pannalal Bombay IV. p. 4. Praśasti Saṁgraha p.. 50-57. R. A. Sastri II. p. 189. Rice p. 318. Śravaṇabelgola 232. TD. 11043 (inc.).
See Jain Ant. XV. i. p. 43; XIX. i. p. 4. Jaina Sid. Bhās. IV. ii. p.. 115. 118. Also under Ugrāditya, NCC. II. p. 284a.
Ed. with Intro. Notes an. Hindi transl. by V. P. Shastri, Sholapur, 1940.

Kalyāṇakāraka
Jain. by Kumārasenadeva. Arrah I. p. 6.

Kalyāṇakāraka
med. ascribed to Devanandin; identified with Pūjyapāda or Jinendrabuddhi; said to be a. authority on Śālākya (surgery). Arrah II. 61.
See also BORI. D. XIX. ii. 687.
It was probably known in Cambodia. Ref. to by Ugrāditya in his [Page251-a. Kalyāṇakāraka; by Pārśvapaṇḍita in Pārśvapurāṇa (Kannada) composed in 1222 A. D. (Karṇātakakavicarite, I. p. 325). Jagadalla Somanātha wrote his Kannada Kalyāṇakāraka on the basis of Pūjyapāda's work.
See Jaina Sid. Bhās. IV. ii. p. 117; XXI. i. p. 26. Jain Ant. XVI. i. p. 4. XVIII. i. p. 10. XIX. i. p. 1. Anekānt II. vii. p. 403. Praśasti Saṁgraha, p.. 49. 53.

Kalyāṇakīrti
Jain. saluted by Amarakīrti in the opening verse of his C. on Dhanañjaya's Nāmamālā.
See Jñānapīṭha edn. Benares 1950, p. 1.

Kalyāṇakīrti
Jain.
--Aṣṭasahasraviṣamapadatātparyasahita. (C.. on Devāgamastotra). Moodbidri II. 149 (inc.).

Kalyāṇadevī

Kalyāṇadevī

Kalyāṇanātha
